solutionSql:
INSERT INTO customer_versions (id, customer_id, region, valid_from, valid_to)
SELECT (SELECT MAX(id) FROM customer_versions) + ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n.customer_id),
       n.customer_id, n.region, n.changed_at, NULL
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.customer_id) r.customer_id, r.region, r.changed_at
  FROM staging_customer_regions AS r
  JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = r.customer_id
  ORDER BY r.customer_id, r.changed_at DESC NULLS LAST
) AS n
JOIN customer_versions AS cur
  ON cur.customer_id = n.customer_id AND cur.valid_to IS NULL
WHERE cur.region IS DISTINCT FROM n.region;
UPDATE customer_versions AS old_row
SET valid_to = new_row.valid_from
FROM customer_versions AS new_row
WHERE new_row.customer_id = old_row.customer_id
  AND old_row.valid_to IS NULL
  AND new_row.valid_to IS NULL
  AND new_row.valid_from > old_row.valid_from;

Customer 2 is skipped because its newest change (South) repeats the current region. Customer 99 is ignored. Each customer has exactly one current row.
ambiguities: New ids "continue after the largest id", but the text does not say the order when one run adds several rows. I numbered them by customer_id (customer 4 gets 17, customer 6 gets 18). The state check compares ids, so this order must be stated.
"Repeats the customer's current region" with NULL on both sides: I treated that as a repeat (IS DISTINCT FROM). No dataset has that case.
The text does not say how to find the previous current row. I used the current row with an older valid_from as the one to close. This gives the same result here.
